properties.title: Hammersmith, London
properties.story: The classically trained musician who joined in 1982 and became the band's studio architect through their imperial phase, from Construction Time Again to Songs of Faith and Devotion.

properties.title: South Woodford, London
properties.story: The founding songwriter behind Dreaming of Me, New Life and Just Can't Get Enough. He left after Speak & Spell to form Yazoo and later Erasure — handing the songwriting torch to Martin Gore.

properties.title: Dagenham, London
properties.story: Born in Dagenham and raised in Basildon, Martin became the band's principal songwriter from 1982 onwards — the pen behind Personal Jesus, Enjoy the Silence, Never Let Me Down Again and nearly everything else.

properties.title: Nottingham
properties.story: Born in Nottingham before his family moved to Basildon, Fletch was the band's heart, diplomat and self-described 'tall guy in the background'. He remained a constant for 42 years until his death in May 2022.

properties.title: Epping, Essex
properties.story: Born in Epping and raised in Basildon, Dave was recruited after Vince Clarke heard him sing Bowie's 'Heroes' at a jam session. He even gave the band its name, borrowed from French fashion magazine Dépêche Mode.

properties.title: Basildon, Essex
properties.story: The Essex new town where Dave Gahan, Martin Gore, Andy Fletcher and Vince Clarke grew up and formed the band in 1980. The town's pedestrian underpasses and brutalist architecture have become pilgrimage sites for fans from around the world.

trivia.curious: Basildon is a post-war 'new town' built to rehouse bombed-out Londoners.
trivia.fan: They tried the name 'Composition of Sound' before Dave Gahan suggested Depeche Mode.
trivia.devotee: Devotees still seek out the brutalist pedestrian underpasses Anton Corbijn would later echo in the band's imagery.

properties.title: St Nicholas School, Basildon
properties.story: After early shows as Composition of Sound, the freshly renamed Depeche Mode played a school gig in Basildon in the autumn of 1980 — Dave Gahan now on vocals, three synths, and a drum machine. Nobody present knew they were watching history.

properties.title: The Bridge House, Canning Town
properties.story: The legendary East London pub venue where the young band played early shows — and where Daniel Miller of Mute Records saw them, leading to the handshake deal that defined their career. The venue closed in 1982; a plaque-worthy spot for any devotee.

properties.title: Mute Records, London
properties.story: Daniel Miller's fiercely independent label signed the band on a handshake and a 50/50 profit split — no contract — and stayed their home for over two decades. One of the great artist-label partnerships in music history.

properties.title: Blackwing Studios, Southwark
properties.summary: The church where synth-pop history was made.
properties.story: Housed in the deconsecrated All Hallows Church in south London, Blackwing is where the first singles and the first two albums took shape — synth-pop history made inside a Victorian church.

trivia.curious: Blackwing was built inside a derelict Victorian church in Southwark.
trivia.fan: Engineer Eric Radcliffe's gear shaped the early Mute sound across Yazoo and DM alike.
trivia.devotee: The building, All Hallows, was bombed in WWII and never reconsecrated — a literal haunted box for synth-pop's birth.

properties.title: Dreaming of Me — debut single
properties.story: Recorded at Blackwing with Daniel Miller producing, the debut single scraped to No. 57 in the UK — enough for Mute to keep going. New Life and Just Can't Get Enough followed within months, and the rocket left the pad.

properties.title: Speak & Spell
properties.story: Recorded at Blackwing and released in October 1981 — bubbly Vince Clarke synth-pop including Just Can't Get Enough. Weeks after release, Clarke announced he was leaving.

trivia.curious: It's named after the Texas Instruments children's toy.
trivia.fan: Vince Clarke wrote nearly all of it, then announced he was leaving weeks after release.
trivia.devotee: The US Sire pressing swapped the tracklist and artwork — early collectors still hunt that variant.

properties.title: BBC Television Centre, London
properties.story: Performing New Life on Top of the Pops in June 1981 put four Basildon teenagers in front of the whole nation. Fletch kept his bank job a little longer — just in case.

trivia.curious: Top of the Pops was the BBC's must-watch weekly chart show.
trivia.fan: Performing 'New Life' on it in 1981 put four Basildon teenagers in front of the whole nation.
trivia.devotee: Fletch kept his day job at an insurance firm for a while even after the TOTP appearance — just in case it all fell apart.

properties.title: The Ritz, New York
properties.story: The band's first US appearance came at Manhattan's The Ritz in January 1982 — a teenage synth band a long way from Essex, planting the first seed of what would become one of America's biggest cult followings.

properties.title: A Broken Frame
properties.story: Recorded at Blackwing as a trio after Vince Clarke's departure, with Martin Gore suddenly chief songwriter. See You and Leave in Silence pointed toward the moodier band to come.

properties.title: Hammersmith Odeon, London
properties.summary: Alan Wilder's era begins on stage.
properties.story: Through 1982 the live band was completed by Alan Wilder, recruited via a Melody Maker ad ('must be under 21' — he wasn't). London theatre shows like Hammersmith captured the moment the boys became a real touring force.

properties.title: Construction Time Again
properties.story: Recorded at The Garden in Shoreditch (John Foxx's studio) and mixed at Hansa Berlin. The band discovered sampling — hitting scrap metal for Pipeline — and Everything Counts gave them their anthem of industry and greed.

properties.title: Hansa Studios, Berlin
properties.story: The band's mid-80s creative home, metres from the Berlin Wall. The Meistersaal's atmosphere — and West Berlin's nightlife — seeped into the darker, industrial textures of the band's imperial phase.

trivia.curious: Hansa Studios sits just metres from where the Berlin Wall once ran.
trivia.fan: Bowie and Iggy Pop recorded here years earlier — the 'Hansa by the Wall' mythology preceded DM.
trivia.devotee: The cavernous Meistersaal's natural reverb is all over 'Stripped' — they miked the room itself, not just the kit.

properties.title: Some Great Reward
properties.summary: People are people — and blasphemous rumours.
properties.story: Largely recorded and mixed at Hansa Berlin. People Are People became their first US hit, Master and Servant scandalised radio, and Somebody proved Martin could break hearts with just a piano.

trivia.curious: It features 'People Are People' and 'Master and Servant'.
trivia.fan: 'Blasphemous Rumours' drew radio controversy for its line about God's sense of humour.
trivia.devotee: For 'Pipeline' they recorded out on a railway embankment, banging real scrap metal — musique concrète smuggled into pop.

properties.title: Black Celebration
properties.story: Recorded at Westside London and Hansa Berlin, Black Celebration is the moment the band's gothic, atmospheric identity fully formed — Stripped, A Question of Lust, and a title track for everyone surviving another day.

trivia.curious: It's widely seen as their first fully 'dark' album.
trivia.fan: The mood split critics at the time but built the devoted cult that followed.
trivia.devotee: 'Stripped' is built around a sampled revving motorbike and the groan of the Hansa studio lift.

properties.title: Music for the Masses
properties.story: Recorded largely at Studio Guillaume Tell near Paris with Dave Bascombe. Never Let Me Down Again, Strangelove and Behind the Wheel armed the tour that ended at the Rose Bowl — the ironic title came true.

trivia.curious: The album's title was deliberately, knowingly ironic.
trivia.fan: It broke them in America, a run that ended in triumph at the Rose Bowl.
trivia.devotee: Corbijn plastered LA with roadside 'MFTM' loudhailer posters carrying no band name at all — pure provocation.

properties.title: Rose Bowl, Pasadena
properties.story: On 18 June 1988, the Music for the Masses tour climaxed in front of roughly 65,000 fans — the band's 101st and final show of the tour, immortalised in D.A. Pennebaker's film and live album '101'. The moment a cult British synth band proved they were a stadium act in America.

trivia.curious: The 101 show was the 101st and final date of the Music for the Masses tour.
trivia.fan: D.A. Pennebaker, who filmed Dylan's 'Dont Look Back', shot it as the documentary '101'.
trivia.devotee: Booking a 60,000-seat stadium for a synth band was a wild gamble — a late KROQ radio push is what got it over the line.

properties.title: Tabernas Desert, Almería
properties.summary: Personal Jesus — a western in Spain.
properties.story: Anton Corbijn shot the Personal Jesus video in Spain's Tabernas Desert, where the spaghetti westerns were filmed — cowboys, horses and a bordello aesthetic for the single that re-invented Depeche Mode with a guitar riff.

properties.title: Puk Studios, Denmark
properties.story: A residential studio in the Danish countryside where much of Violator was crafted, with Flood co-producing and Alan Wilder pushing the band's sound design to new heights.

properties.title: Violator
properties.story: Begun at Logic Studios in Milan, continued at Puk in Denmark and mixed in London. Personal Jesus, Enjoy the Silence, Policy of Truth, World in My Eyes — the album this very app is named after, and the band's creative and commercial peak.

trivia.fan: The title was a tongue-in-cheek joke about over-the-top heavy-metal album names.
trivia.devotee: There is no song called 'Violator' — and Corbijn's lone rose on the sleeve was a deliberate nod to beauty hiding menace.

properties.title: Swiss Alps
properties.story: Anton Corbijn filmed Dave Gahan wandering mountain landscapes as a king carrying a deckchair for the Enjoy the Silence video — shot across the Swiss Alps, Portugal and the Scottish Highlands. One of the most iconic music videos ever made.

trivia.curious: Dave plays a crown-wearing king wandering with a deckchair.
trivia.fan: Martin wrote it as a slow ballad; Alan Wilder and Flood rebuilt it as a dance track overnight.
trivia.devotee: The king's stroll was filmed across the Swiss Alps, the Scottish Highlands AND Portugal — geographic continuity be damned.

properties.title: Tower Records, Sunset Strip
properties.story: A planned in-store signing for Violator in March 1990 drew an estimated 17,000+ fans to West Hollywood, overwhelming police and making the evening news. Proof of just how big the band had become in the US.

properties.title: Giants Stadium, New Jersey
properties.summary: World Violation conquers the East Coast.
properties.story: The World Violation Tour sold out Giants Stadium — around 80,000 tickets gone in hours — alongside multiple nights at Dodger Stadium in LA. Violator-era Depeche Mode were, by any measure, one of the biggest bands on Earth.

properties.title: Madrid
properties.summary: Songs of Faith and Devotion begins.
properties.story: The band rented a villa in Madrid and converted it into a studio to begin Songs of Faith and Devotion — famously tense sessions, a band fraying at the edges, yet producing some of their most powerful music.

properties.title: Songs of Faith and Devotion
properties.summary: Grunge-era gospel. A UK and US No. 1.
properties.story: Built in the Madrid villa and finished in Hamburg and London, SOFAD debuted at No. 1 on both sides of the Atlantic. I Feel You, Walking in My Shoes, Condemnation — the sound of a band tearing itself apart and making it sing.

properties.title: Crystal Palace Bowl, London
properties.story: On 31 July 1993, the Devotional Tour played its great London open-air show at Crystal Palace Bowl. The tour was later described as 'the most debauched rock'n'roll tour in history' — and the music was extraordinary.

properties.title: Johannesburg, South Africa
properties.summary: The Exotic Tour goes where no tour had gone.
properties.story: The 1994 Exotic Tour took the Devotional show to South Africa, South America, Hawaii and Southeast Asia — first-ever shows on several continents, with a band running on fumes. Alan Wilder left the following year.

properties.title: Ultra
properties.story: Recorded with Tim Simenon at Eastcote in London and studios in LA and New York, as a trio and against the odds — Dave newly clean after nearly dying in 1996. Barrel of a Gun and It's No Good announced the band had survived itself.

properties.title: Tartu, Estonia
properties.summary: The Singles Tour opens behind the old Iron Curtain.
properties.story: The Singles Tour 86>98 opened in Tartu, Estonia in September 1998 — a nod to the band's enormous Eastern European following, where bootleg tapes had made them folk heroes long before they could play there.

properties.title: Exciter
properties.story: Produced by LFO's Mark Bell, with sessions at RAK in London and studios in Santa Barbara and New York. Dream On and I Feel Loved took the band into the new century with a quieter kind of confidence.

properties.title: Santa Barbara, California
properties.summary: The band's West Coast home base.
properties.story: From the mid-2000s, much of every album took shape in Santa Barbara, where Martin Gore settled — at Sound Design and later his home studio, wonderfully named Electric Ladyboy. The Essex boys' story now runs through Californian sunshine.

properties.title: Playing the Angel
properties.summary: Pain and suffering in various tempos.
properties.story: Recorded in Santa Barbara and New York with Ben Hillier. Precious returned them to the top 10 worldwide, and for the first time Dave Gahan contributed songs — including Suffer Well.

properties.title: Forum di Assago, Milan
properties.summary: Touring the Angel: Live in Milan.
properties.story: The Touring the Angel shows at Milan's Forum were filmed for the celebrated live DVD — Italy's famously devoted fanbase providing one of the loudest crowds the band ever recorded.

properties.title: Sounds of the Universe
properties.story: Martin bought a trove of vintage analogue gear online and the band built the album around it in Santa Barbara and New York. Wrong gave them one of their strangest, darkest singles — and videos.

properties.title: Ramat Gan Stadium, Tel Aviv
properties.summary: Tour of the Universe lifts off.
properties.story: The Tour of the Universe opened in Tel Aviv in May 2009. Days later Dave was diagnosed with a bladder tumour, forcing postponements — he recovered, and the tour went on to play to over 2.7 million people.

properties.title: Palau Sant Jordi, Barcelona
properties.summary: Tour of the Universe: Barcelona — the live film.
properties.story: The November 2009 Barcelona shows were filmed for the Tour of the Universe live album and film — Spain's fervent fanbase captured in full voice for posterity.

properties.title: Delta Machine
properties.story: Recorded in Santa Barbara and at Jungle City in New York with Ben Hillier. Heaven and Should Be Higher leaned into the gospel-blues undercurrent that had always run beneath the synths.

properties.title: Stade de France, Paris
properties.summary: The Delta Machine Tour at full scale.
properties.story: The 2013–14 Delta Machine Tour filled Europe's biggest stadiums, including the Stade de France — three decades on from Blackwing, still growing.

properties.title: Spirit
properties.story: Recorded in Santa Barbara and New York with James Ford producing — the band's angriest, most political record since the 80s, released into a world that had caught up with its warnings.

properties.title: Friends Arena, Stockholm
properties.story: The Global Spirit Tour opened in Stockholm in May 2017 and went on to reach more than 3 million people — at the time one of the highest-attended tours in the world.

properties.title: Waldbühne, Berlin
properties.story: The Global Spirit tour closed with celebrated 2018 Waldbühne shows in Berlin — the city that shaped the band's sound — filmed for the SPiRiTS in the Forest documentary, a love letter to the fans themselves.

properties.title: Rock & Roll Hall of Fame, Cleveland
properties.story: In 2020, Depeche Mode were inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame — formal recognition, four decades in, that the synthesizer band from Basildon changed popular music.

properties.title: Memento Mori
properties.summary: Remember you must die — so live.
properties.story: Largely written before Andy Fletcher's death in May 2022 and recorded in Santa Barbara and New York with James Ford. Ghosts Again gave the band their most beloved single in years; the album is dedicated to Fletch's memory.

trivia.curious: The title is Latin for 'remember you must die'.
trivia.fan: Much of it was written before Fletch's death and finished after.
trivia.devotee: Several songs predate the pandemic — the 'remember death' theme was chosen, unnervingly, before the losses arrived.

properties.title: Golden 1 Center, Sacramento
properties.story: On 23 March 2023, Dave and Martin opened the Memento Mori world tour — the first without Andy Fletcher, whose memory the tour honoured nightly. It became one of the highest-grossing tours of the band's career.

properties.title: Twickenham Stadium, London
properties.story: In June 2023 the Memento Mori tour came home to London's 80,000-capacity Twickenham Stadium — Basildon boys, 43 years on, still filling the biggest stages in their own country.

properties.title: Bilbao, Spain
properties.summary: The final show of Memento Mori.
properties.story: The Memento Mori world tour closed in Bilbao in April 2024 after 112 shows across the globe — the end of the band's most emotional tour, and (for now) the latest chapter of the story.

properties.title: Yazoo — Upstairs at Eric's
properties.story: Within weeks of leaving Depeche Mode, Vince Clarke was back at Blackwing with Alison Moyet recording Yazoo's debut — named after engineer Eric Radcliffe's upstairs room. Only You and Don't Go came out of the very building where Speak & Spell was made.

trivia.curious: Yazoo was Vince Clarke's duo with singer Alison Moyet.
trivia.fan: It was recorded in the same Blackwing church that birthed DM's debut.
trivia.devotee: Vince and Alison first connected through Melody Maker small ads; the album is named for Blackwing's Eric Radcliffe — 'Upstairs at Eric's'.

properties.title: The Assembly — Never Never
properties.story: Vince Clarke and Blackwing's Eric Radcliffe planned a project with a different singer on every release. They managed one: Never Never with Feargal Sharkey, a UK No. 4 — then Vince met Andy Bell and Erasure happened instead.

properties.title: Erasure forms in London
properties.story: Vince Clarke auditioned singers through a Melody Maker ad; Andy Bell was the 42nd hopeful. Wonderland followed in 1986, and Erasure became one of Britain's most enduring pop acts — still going four decades later.

properties.title: Recoil — The Thin Line, Sussex
properties.story: After leaving Depeche Mode in 1995, Alan Wilder made Recoil his full-time vehicle, recording dark, cinematic albums like Unsound Methods and subHuman at his Sussex home studio, The Thin Line.

properties.title: Martin L. Gore — Counterfeit²
properties.story: Martin's solo outlet has always been covers and instrumentals — the Counterfeit EPs and later the MG and Third Chimpanzee albums, made at his Santa Barbara home studio. The writer of hundreds of songs, relaxing in other people's.

properties.title: Dave Gahan — Paper Monsters
properties.story: Dave's solo debut, written and recorded in New York where he'd rebuilt his life. Its success changed Depeche Mode itself — from Playing the Angel onwards, Gahan songs appear on every album.

properties.title: Dave Gahan & Soulsavers
properties.story: Dave's ongoing collaboration with production duo Soulsavers — The Light the Dead See, Angels & Ghosts and Imposter — recorded largely in Los Angeles, gave his voice its most soulful setting outside the Mode.

properties.title: Croc's, Rayleigh
properties.story: The crocodile-themed Rayleigh club (later the Pink Toothbrush) where the fledgling band played a near-weekly residency in 1980–81, building the local following that carried them to London.

properties.title: Vince Clarke leaves
properties.summary: The songwriter walks, weeks after the debut.
properties.story: In November 1981, with Speak & Spell still climbing the charts, Vince Clarke announced he was leaving. Most bands would have died on the spot; instead, 20-year-old Martin Gore picked up the pen.

properties.title: Just Can't Get Enough — single
properties.story: Recorded at Blackwing and released in September 1981, Vince Clarke's bubblegum masterpiece became the band's first top-10 hit — and forty years on, a football-terrace anthem sung by people who couldn't name the band.

properties.title: Alan Wilder joins
properties.story: Answering a Melody Maker ad seeking a synth player (under 21 only — Alan was 22), the classically trained Wilder auditioned in London and got the gig. He became the sonic architect of the band's greatest records.

properties.title: US Festival, San Bernardino
properties.summary: Playing to a sea of confused Californians.
properties.story: On 'New Wave Day' at the 1983 US Festival, the young band played to one of the biggest crowds of their life in the California desert — an early, surreal taste of the American scale to come.

properties.title: HMS Belfast, London
properties.summary: People Are People — filmed on a warship.
properties.story: The video for the band's first US hit was shot aboard HMS Belfast on the Thames, its industrial clanks and naval guns matching the track's metal-bashing samples.

trivia.curious: It was filmed aboard HMS Belfast, moored on the Thames.
trivia.fan: The song became their first US Top 20 hit.
trivia.devotee: Its metallic clangs were sampled from the warship and the studio — they literally bashed the set they were filming on.

properties.title: Alsterdorfer Sporthalle, Hamburg
properties.summary: The World We Live In and Live in Hamburg.
properties.story: The Some Great Reward tour's Hamburg stop was filmed for the band's first concert video — early proof of the German devotion that would define their career.

properties.title: Tokyo, Japan
properties.story: The band's first Japanese dates in April 1985 opened up yet another devoted territory — the start of a relationship with Japan that continues to this day.

properties.title: Personal Jesus — single
properties.story: Built around a blues guitar riff at Logic Studios in Milan and teased via newspaper ads reading 'Your own personal Jesus' with a phone number, it became one of the most covered songs in the catalogue — Johnny Cash and Marilyn Manson included.

trivia.curious: It was inspired by Priscilla Presley's memoir about life with Elvis.
trivia.fan: Mute ran cryptic newspaper ads — 'Your own personal Jesus' with a phone number — before anyone knew it was DM.
trivia.devotee: Call that ad's number and you actually heard the single down the line; the stunt jammed switchboards across Britain.

properties.title: Enjoy the Silence — single
properties.story: Martin wrote it as a slow ballad; Alan Wilder and Flood heard a dance track at Puk Studios and rebuilt it overnight. The result won the 1991 BRIT for Best Single and remains the band's defining song.

properties.title: Scottish Highlands
properties.story: The Scottish leg of Anton Corbijn's Enjoy the Silence shoot — Dave's wandering king crossing the Highlands with his deckchair, a long way from his kingdom.

properties.title: Dodger Stadium, Los Angeles
properties.story: Two sold-out nights at Dodger Stadium in August 1990 — around 90,000 tickets — confirmed Los Angeles as the band's American heartland, two years after the Rose Bowl.

properties.title: Madison Square Garden, New York
properties.summary: A New York institution, era after era.
properties.story: From World Violation in 1990 through Tour of the Universe and Memento Mori, the Garden became the band's New York home — a venue they've filled across five decades.

properties.title: Stade Couvert, Liévin
properties.story: Anton Corbijn filmed the Devotional concert film at the band's December 1993 shows in this northern French arena — the band at their darkest, heaviest and, many fans argue, their absolute live peak.

properties.title: Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
properties.summary: The Exotic Tour reaches South America.
properties.story: January 1994 festival shows in Brazil brought the Devotional set to South America for the first time — another continent claimed by the Exotic Tour's exhausted, brilliant band.

properties.title: Alan Wilder leaves
properties.story: In June 1995, after the punishing Devotional era, Alan Wilder announced his departure, citing years of unequal workload. The band continued as a trio; he returned just once — joining Martin for Somebody at Royal Albert Hall in 2010.

properties.title: Adrenalin Village, London
properties.story: With no tour possible after Dave's recovery, Ultra launched with two 'Ultra Parties' — London and Los Angeles. Short sets, huge relief: Depeche Mode still existed.

properties.title: Morocco
properties.summary: Barrel of a Gun — Corbijn in North Africa.
properties.story: Anton Corbijn shot the fevered, eye-painted Barrel of a Gun video in Morocco — the dark, disorientating image of the band's resurrection record.

properties.title: Palais Omnisports de Paris-Bercy
properties.story: The Exciter Tour's Paris stop was filmed by Anton Corbijn as 'One Night in Paris' — elegant, stripped back, and proof the band had grown into their third decade with style intact.

properties.title: Downtown Los Angeles
properties.story: A masked man strapped in a car rolling backwards through downtown LA at dawn — the unsettling, award-nominated Wrong video became one of the band's most talked-about late-era moments.

properties.title: Marigny Opera House, New Orleans
properties.summary: Heaven — filmed in a ruined church.
properties.story: Timothy Saccenti shot the Heaven video in the candle-lit, deconsecrated Marigny Opera House — gospel atmosphere for Delta Machine's lead single, in the city that invented the mood.

properties.title: O2 World, Berlin
properties.story: Anton Corbijn filmed the Delta Machine tour's Berlin nights for the 'Live in Berlin' film and album — the band returning, as always, to the city that shaped them.

properties.title: Foro Sol, Mexico City
properties.story: Mexico City's enormous Foro Sol shows — tens of thousands singing every word — cemented Mexico as one of the band's most passionate territories, revisited on every tour since.

properties.title: Remembering Fletch
properties.story: Andy Fletcher died at home in London in May 2022, aged 60. The band's heart and quiet diplomat for 42 years, he was honoured nightly on the Memento Mori tour — 'Fletch would have loved this song.'

trivia.curious: Andy 'Fletch' Fletcher died in May 2022, aged 60.
trivia.fan: Fletch quietly ran much of the band's business affairs alongside playing keyboards.
trivia.devotee: He once summed up his role with total honesty: 'Martin's the songwriter, Dave's the vocalist, and I bum around.'

properties.title: Ghosts Again — single
properties.story: Written with Richard Butler of the Psychedelic Furs and recorded in Santa Barbara, Ghosts Again gave the two-piece Depeche Mode their most beloved single in a decade — melancholy, danceable, defiantly alive.

trivia.curious: It was the lead single from Memento Mori (2023).
trivia.fan: It was co-written with Richard Butler of the Psychedelic Furs.
trivia.devotee: Martin had the music before Fletch died; its eerie serenity ended up reframing the whole album as a goodbye.

properties.title: New York rooftops
properties.summary: Ghosts Again — chess with death, gently.
properties.story: Anton Corbijn filmed Dave and Martin playing rooftop chess in New York — a tender Seventh Seal nod for a song about mortality, made by two men who had just lost their oldest friend.

properties.title: VCMG — Ssss
properties.story: Thirty years after Vince walked out, Clarke and Gore made a full-on techno album together for Mute — almost entirely by swapping files, barely in the same room. The most Depeche Mode reunion imaginable.

properties.title: Logic Studios, Milan
properties.story: Early in 1989 the band decamped to Milan's Logic Studios to begin Violator with producer Flood. Personal Jesus took shape here before the sessions moved north to Puk in Denmark — the first sparks of their masterpiece.

properties.title: Westside Studios, London
properties.story: Much of Black Celebration was tracked at Westside in west London before mixing at Hansa. The album where Depeche Mode fully embraced the dark — Stripped, A Question of Time, and the title-track dread that defined a generation of fans.

properties.title: Wembley Arena, London
properties.story: Across the Music for the Masses, World Violation and Devotional tours, Wembley Arena was the band's London stronghold — sweaty, ecstatic nights that turned a generation of British kids into lifelong devotees.

properties.title: Pinkpop Festival, Netherlands
properties.story: A blazing 1984 Pinkpop set in Landgraaf helped cement the Low Countries as Depeche Mode heartland — a devotion that has never cooled across four decades of return visits.

properties.title: Rock Werchter, Belgium
properties.story: The twin Torhout–Werchter festival in the summer of 1984 put the young band in front of vast Belgian crowds — another European territory won by sheer relentless touring.

properties.title: Buenos Aires, Argentina
properties.summary: The Exotic Tour hits South America.
properties.story: On the punishing 1994 Exotic Tour, Depeche Mode reached Argentina for the first time — a continent of new devotees discovered just as the band was burning itself to the ground. The fans never forgot.

properties.title: World in My Eyes — single
properties.summary: Let me take you on a trip.
properties.story: The final single from Violator, recorded at Puk in Denmark — Martin Gore's hymn to intimacy and travel. "Let me take you on a trip": the song that gives this atlas its name and its spirit.

trivia.curious: It was the fourth and final single from Violator.
trivia.fan: Its opening line, 'let me take you on a trip', gives this very atlas its name.
trivia.devotee: Its remixes — the dub-heavy 'Oil Tank' cut among them — made it a club staple far beyond the album.

properties.title: Strangelove video, Paris
properties.story: Anton Corbijn shot Strangelove in moody monochrome Paris — the beginning of a creative partnership that would shape the band's entire visual identity for the next forty years.

properties.title: It's No Good video, Las Vegas
properties.summary: Dave as the lounge act from hell.
properties.story: Corbijn cast Dave Gahan as a washed-up Vegas crooner playing to empty tables — gloriously self-aware comedy from a band that had just stared down the abyss and lived to laugh about it.
